source_binding.paper: Four-Coloring P6-Free Graphs. II. Finding an Excellent Precoloring
facts: Axiom (iv): no vertex outside Y0 union X0 is mixed on an edge of Y0.
Acceptability is defined on nonadjacent y,y' in Y intersect N(Y0), unequal lists, and an extension coloring both from their list intersection.
In the acceptability proof, common-neighbor witnesses are chosen only after y,y' and the extension premise are fixed.

fixed_context: One ordered type pair (T,T'), one stored 111 state (p,m,n), one post-Lemma10 descendant P'.

definitions.Sigma: Sigma(v)={C in CC : v is complete to C}
definitions.A: {y in Y'(T) intersect N(Y0') : ym is a nonedge}
definitions.B: {y' in Y'(T') intersect N(Y0') : y'm is an edge}
definitions.R_C11: {(y,y') in A x B : yy' is a nonedge and Sigma(y) intersect Sigma(y') is nonempty}

S1_COMPONENT_UNIFORMITY.claim: For every v in Y' and every connected component C of G[Y0'], v is either complete or anticomplete to C.
proof: v lies outside Y0' union X0'.
Descendant axiom (iv) forbids v from being mixed on any edge of Y0'.
Along any edge ab of C, adjacency of v to a and b must agree.
Connectivity propagates this equality along every path in C.
Therefore adjacency is constant across C.

S2_COMMON_WITNESS_EQUIVALENCE.claim: N(y) intersect N(y') intersect Y0' is nonempty iff Sigma(y) intersect Sigma(y') is nonempty.
proof: If z is a common witness, let C be its Y0' component. By S1 both y and y' are complete to C, so C lies in both signatures.
Conversely, if C lies in both signatures, every z in C is adjacent to both y and y', so a common witness exists.

S3_RELATION_REPRESENTATION.claim: After exact z-fiber quotient, the graph-discoverable survivor family is exactly the binary relation R_C11 on A x B.
proof: The z-fiber theorem removes the identity of a common witness while preserving the ordered pair (y,y').
S2 replaces existence of any common witness by the graph-only signature-intersection predicate.
The remaining structural conditions are precisely y in A, y' in B, and yy' nonedge.

S4_CERTIFICATE_ONLY_COMPONENT_IDENTITY.claim: A common component C in Sigma(y) intersect Sigma(y') is a graph certificate for relation membership, not an additional answer-relevant coordinate.
proof: Answer relevance and the exact {3,4}^2 extension projection are functions of the fixed pair (y,y') in the fixed P'.
The z-fiber theorem already proves witness identity irrelevant.
Replacing a vertex witness z by its containing common component records only why the graph predicate holds.

relation_object.graph_predicate: yy' nonedge AND Sigma(y) intersect Sigma(y') nonempty

nonclaims: Equal Sigma signatures do not imply equal extension projections.
No distinct survivor pairs are identified.
No bound g(|S|) on |R_C11| is proved.
No bounded hitting set is proved.
No repair or new descriptor is defined.
